crags.name: Index Town Wall
reasons: Very high humidity (96%) — rock stays damp

nws.forecast: Patchy fog and rain and snow. Mostly cloudy. High near 40, with temperatures falling to around 38 in the afternoon. West northwest wind around 2 mph. Chance of precipitation is 90%. New rainfall amounts less than a tenth of an inch possible.

crag_meta.notes: Granite dries fast. Lower Wall sheds water quickly; Upper Wall slower after heavy rain.

crags.name: Leavenworth
reasons: Very high humidity (97%) — rock stays damp

nws.forecast: Snow likely before 3pm, then rain likely. Mostly cloudy, with a high near 37. Northwest wind around 5 mph. Chance of precipitation is 70%. New snow accumulation of around one inch possible.

crag_meta.notes: Rain shadow effect — dries significantly faster than west-side crags. Icicle Canyon blocks moisture.

crags.name: Vantage
reasons: Very high humidity (89%) — rock stays damp

nws.forecast: Rain likely. Mostly cloudy. High near 52, with temperatures falling to around 49 in the afternoon. Northwest wind around 9 mph. Chance of precipitation is 70%. New rainfall amounts less than a tenth of an inch possible.

crag_meta.notes: Desert climate, basalt dries fast. Wind is a major factor — often climbable when west-side crags are soaked.

crags.name: Little Si
reasons: Very high humidity (98%) — rock stays damp

alerts.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued March 13 at 8:20AM PDT until March 13 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS Seattle WA

crag_meta.notes: Wetter microclimate than Index. Higher humidity typical. Needs more drying time.

crags.name: Mt. Erie
reasons: Very high humidity (89%) — rock stays damp

nws.forecast: A chance of rain and snow before noon, then a chance of rain and snow between noon and 2pm. Mostly cloudy. High near 44, with temperatures falling to around 42 in the afternoon. West wind around 3 mph. Chance of precipitation is 40%. New rainfall amounts between a tenth and quarter of an inch possible.

crag_meta.notes: Island climate — high humidity, slow drying. Needs 48h+ after rain to be reliable.

crags.name: Peshastin Pinnacles
reasons: Sandstone — never climb wet, damages rock
Very high humidity (99%) — rock stays damp

alerts.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued March 13 at 11:29AM PDT until March 13 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA

nws.forecast: Snow before 4pm, then rain and snow. Cloudy. High near 43, with temperatures falling to around 40 in the afternoon. Northwest wind around 5 mph. Chance of precipitation is 90%. New snow accumulation of less than half an inch possible.

crag_meta.notes: Sandstone — NEVER climb when wet. Holds water in pockets, damages rock when damp. Needs 48-72h after rain.

crags.name: Exit 38
reasons: Very high humidity (94%) — rock stays damp

alerts.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued March 13 at 8:20AM PDT until March 14 at 5:00AM PDT by NWS Seattle WA

nws.forecast: Areas of fog and rain and snow before 1pm, then areas of fog and rain and snow. Cloudy. High near 37, with temperatures falling to around 35 in the afternoon. West northwest wind around 2 mph. Chance of precipitation is 100%. New rainfall amounts between a quarter and half of an inch possible.

crag_meta.notes: Closest sport climbing to Seattle. Metamorphic andesite dries slower than granite. Many walls face north or are shaded by forest — factor in extra drying time. Deception Crags is most popular; Far Side and Mt Washington have longer approaches.

crags.name: Castle Rock
reasons: Very high humidity (93%) — rock stays damp

crag_meta.notes: Southwest-facing granite in Tumwater Canyon. Gets afternoon sun, dries reasonably fast. Home to Washington's first multipitch technical rock climb (Midway, 1948). Rock is polished from heavy traffic — friction matters more when damp.

nws.forecast: A chance of rain after 2pm. Mostly cloudy. High near 57, with temperatures falling to around 55 in the afternoon. Southwest wind around 16 mph, with gusts as high as 28 mph. Chance of precipitation is 30%.

crag_meta.notes: High desert volcanic tuff dries fast and the climate is much drier than PNW. Often climbable year-round. Watch for seasonal raptor closures (Feb-Aug on some walls). Juniper Basin area dries fastest.

The big one. Massive south-facing granite wall — beautiful in good conditions but very slow to dry due to size and coastal moisture. Seeps can persist for days after heavy rain. Upper Chief dries slower than the base. Check the access society for any closures before heading up.

The local's playground — lower elevation, well-traveled, and significantly faster-drying than The Chief. Often climbable a day after rain clears when the Chief is still weeping. Varied aspects mean some walls see sun most of the day. One of the best urban crags in North America.
Deep forest setting, slow drying. 6 sub-areas: Morpheus, Paradise, Prospect, Hideout, Jungle Gym, Apex. 205 problems. Needs significant dry time after rain.
